Speaker(s): Ash Kyd, Glen Arrowsmith, Kory Nunn

Title: Techniques and practices for testing Angular 2
Ionic framework dev with Cloud9 IDE - An intern's perspective
Angular 2 Routing from 0 to Hero
Description: This headline talk promises to show you everything there is to know about routing your next angular 2 app, or give you know familiarity to navigate anyone's project. Covering setting up, nesting routes and security just to name a few, this bills itself as a one stop demo.

Title: Machine Vision / AI in Electron
Description: Matt has been busy using electron to do AI experiments this year (working on new machine vision algorithms) and has volunteered to share and explain the state of machine vision.

Title: React Native
Description: Ryan actually started off volunteering to talk to us about Cordova and PhoneGap some time ago, but as our community does... we discover so much tech in such a short time. In demonstration of this... Ryan will be able to present React Native, and explain some common pitfalls and lay down what you need to know.

Title: Control your home with HomeBridge & iPhone
Description: Chris has turned into quite a carryover-champ of BrisJS, presenting 3 topics in short succession of the IoT space; wowing the crowds with Slack connected toasters and more. This time he's back to show you the HomeBridge project (npm installable), and how you can set up a simple bit of config and JS to command devices from your iOS/Apple products with homekit too.

Title: Magikcraft
Description: While Josh couldn't make it to give us the original talk Tim Marwick, Ian Daniel & Briggsy stepped up to the plate to walk us through how Magikcraft works and their lofty goal of setting a world record.

Title: Node Debugging Revisited
Description: Node now ships with V8 Inspector integrations so you can use the Chrome DevTools. Glen will cover some basic debugging, logging, performance debugging with flame graphs and more. It could save your life! ...or just your sanity.

Title: Startup Projects from a Tech Perspective
Description: Chris seems to have been enjoying the time honoured tradition of taking a food-snap/foodstagram/food-selfie. But in true developer style - this was a learning opportunity to build an app with some handy technologies, and he can tell us all about this journey mixing the MEAN stack with AWS and Ionic 2... making taking pics of your food cool again ;-)

Title: Building an Alexa Skill with Node + Lambda
Description: John built a version of chaos monkey that allows you to start and stop servers on the Amazon Echo. He'll walk through building a skill that allows you to ask Alexa when the next BrisJS meetup is on using the meetup.com api.

Title: Serverless Express
Description: This talk will step through how to use the aws-serverless-express library to develop a simple API backed by DyamoDB, and how to deploy it to AWS via CloudFormation. In this way you can build web services with Node.js + express and run them through the Amazon API Gateway.

Title: Less is more. Writing software the unpopular way
Description: Kory will be running us through the other way to write software, the one where you don't use frameworks, build processes, or install a million libraries. There are pro's 'n' con's to both, and it will surely be an awesome debate on the merits of each!

Title: WebAssembly 101
Description: Ash is going to blow us away and present his intro on our latest toy... I mean, tool… for this expanding web universe of ours. WebAssembly has landed in Firefox and Chrome with Edge to follow shortly, so with Ash's help we can get started by learning what is it, why we need it, how it works, and how to get a jump on coding with it today.

Title: State Mutation considered harmful: Pure Function Master Race
Description: Functional programming is the One True Way(tm) to code - except when it's not. In this talk we'll look at functional programming in JavaScript, with some use cases and considerations. We're not going to do Monads and Endofunctors, grow a beard, and write a parser, but we will cover some practical use cases in JavaScript.

Title: Simplifying user interface programming
Description: Focused around Liams thoughts on simplifying user interface programming, with examples in React and Redux. Imagine a user interface generated entirely from data. The only way to change the UI is to change the data. Add a simple event system to translate user actions into changes to the data and you have the simple, complete way to construct user interfaces that has made React so popular.

Title: ⚡ Talk: magikcraft, particles.js & more
Description: A last minute entry, Tim will talk about magikcraft, particles.js & more.

Title: React Native
Description: By taking us through his experiences in developing out React Native code in the workplace we'll learn how to get up and running productively with React Native.

Title: GraphQL + Relay.js
Description: Josh worked with the Facebook engineering team around Relay and will be able to give us a good explanation around the concepts of requests describing the data and show GraphQL via graphql.org/swapi-graphql/ and delve into the details of Relay at length.

Title: MCT1: Minecraft for Type 1 Diabetes
Description: MCT1 is a global open-source project that produces a version of Minecraft specifically engineered to make a difference for children and families living with Type 1 Diabetes.

Title: Building an ExpressJS + GraphQL Server
Description: Tim has volunteered a variant talk to follow up from Josh Duck's Relay.js talk last month. What is GraphQL & why is it cool... as well as getting started quickly with Express and GraphQL by the use of a pluggable provider architecture.

Title: Create a website by email
Description: Matt volunteered to take us through how the stack for publishthis.email works. We use SES -> S3 -> Lambda -> Dynamo to convert any email sent to a particular address into a webpage.

Title: Redux
Description: Answering the call to cover this buzzing topic, David will take us through the pattern and implementation of Redux so we can apply it.

Title: Blocking JS + Event Loop + Async
Description: Now recovered from illness, Kory is reprising his much loved JS fundamentals series from years ago. This is a new section explaining another core tenet of JavaScript's operation: how does JS do async flow if it can't natively do async? The dilemma will be explained!

Title: Magikcraft's "JavaScript Über Alles" Tour of Europe
Description: Fresh from speaking at NDC Oslo, setting a new JavaScript world record, and launching the Magikcraft Open Source Platform at CoderDojo's Coolest Projects in Dublin, Ireland, the legendary Josh Wulf presents a wrap-up of the trials, the triumphs, the revolutionary technology, and the life-changing movement that is Magikcraft: introducing a new generation of coders to the power of JavaScript through Minecraft. You will laugh, you will cry, you will be deeply moved by this touching story of the human impact of the world's one true full-stack language: JavaScript.

Title: Internet of JavaScript Things - Automate your life with MongooseOS and mJS
Description: The Internet of Things (IoT) is the third computing revolution, the story so far being Personal computing, Cloud computing and now Ubiquitous computing (IoT). The most annoying challenges in the Internet of Things (IoT) are connecting Things to the cloud safely, managing your Things, and updating them. Mongoose-OS is the new hotness that solves all these problems for you out of the box, and lets you skip ahead to the cool stuff.

Title: Async and await in JavaScript VS promises VS callback
Description: JavaScript is a naturally asynchronous language, but these days there's several ways of doing the same thing. Alberto Falchi will be joining us to discuss the varieties of asynchronous techniques, when to use one or the other… and why!

Title: Create, Debug & Deploy JavaScript Azure Functions
Description: What's serverless? And why would you go serverless? Worry no more, these questions will be answered, as Thiago shows us a great way to get started by using Azure Functions. You don't need to move all your applications to the cloud right now, you can start with bits and pieces without compromising your existing applications and see for yourself how great it can be.

Title: Scaffolding JS stacks using Yeoman, Cloud 66, Docker and pushing to Cloud
Description: This is a talk about how fast we can build up most JS stacks using Yeoman, utilise Docker, choose the cloud provider we like and orchestrate our containers using Cloud 66.

Title: Building a chatbot with AWS Lambda and Lex
Description: John built a chatbot using AWS Lambda (Nodejs of course) and AWS Lex for the AWS Chatbot Challenge - see his blog - https://devpost.com/software/a-cloud-guru-bot-ryfwn3.  John will walk through building a Slack bot and using AWS Lex to add intelligence to the bot. He will touch on AWS Lambda & the Serverless framework.

Title: Reflex - higher-order FRP for front-end development.
Description: There has been a lot of buzz about Functional Reactive Programming over the last few years.  Most of it has been about distant relatives of the original idea, which aren't anywhere near as powerful. This talk will be about Reflex, a Haskell library which uses FRP for  front-end development with great correctness, composability and  performance. Even if you're never going to touch Haskell with a ten-foot pole, the  ideas should be interesting for those who have been following the  various reactive technologies.

Title: Google Docs as a GraphQL backend
Description: A lightning talk by Tim Marwick, showing how he's using Google Sheets as a backend to his GraphQL API. Crazy stuff!

Title: Deploying to the cloud with now.sh
Description: Spur of the moment lightning talk from Kory Nunn showing off how to deploy stuff with "now". Hilarious as always.

Title: Crash course in D3
Description: Josh is a developer for ABC News in Brisbane and has recently learned how to use D3. In this 10 minute video he shows us how to make a spinning globe from scratch in D3.

Title: Node and .NET in-process interop
Description: Recently Kim Burgess had a project where they needed to integrate some of their front-end components (written in js) with another product. Tiny problem - the only integration option for this other product was a .NET SDK!  Faced with the option of having to re-implement one side of this, the thought occurred: why not use both? This talk will be how this was done, why it was done and some tools if others face a similar situation.

Title: Why your legal dept HATES React
Speaker(s): Developer Steve, Thomas McCarthy, Jonathan Lewis
Description: Developer Steven "Steve" Cooper has invited patent and trade mark attorney Jonathan Lewis and developer Thomas McCarthy to discuss the legal side of the React license controversy.  As this is a topic that covers a much wider issue around open source IP ownership and things that growing projects may not always be aware of this panel should be interesting from the legal side and the development side.  This is a panel discussion rather than a straight talk, so there will be an emphasis on audience participation. If you're a React user or generally interested in the project, think about any questions you'd like to throw to the panel on the night and you'll get your chance to ask them.

Title: Themeable email templates with MJML
Description: Who likes making email templates? Not me! But this month Ben is  going to teach us how to build a complete brandable email templating  solution that doesn't suck.

Title: The theme is CSS in JS
Description: Nowadays we write our css in .js files. Howdathunkit? Lets explore the future of writing reusable ui components for our web  apps, by stopping to take a look at the history of css-in-js. Its not a  very long history... but it's crammed full of hacks & innovation  from all corners of our web community! Also, since theming is often vital to successful styling, we'll jump  into some code to discover patterns to enable the overriding of styles  used inside of ui components. The talk is being given by the unknown web lurker & js fanboy,  Lochlan Bunn. Lochy has been writing reusable components, with various  levels of failure, at the local product house Rex Labs.

Title: Anna Gerber Presents: the great Typescript Debate
Speaker(s): Anna Gerber, Kory Nunn, Josh Wulf
Description: TypeScript: Handy Helper, or Harmful Hindrance. This month Kory  and Josh will duke it out for and against TypeScript and strongly typed  languages!   Should Javascript proper support types? Does a compilation step  ruin all the fun? Why are we arguing? Prepare all your burning  questions to ask our caped crusaders on the night.

Title: Lightning talk: What is NodeGirls
Description: If you haven't heard yet, we have a proper NodeGirls chapter in Brisbane now - and there's plenty to get involved with. Anwesha can give you a quick 5 min rundown on the who the when and the what of Brisbane NodeGirls. https://www.facebook.com/NodeGirlsAustralia/ https://www.facebook.com/events/1542779579149962/ - Dec event

Title: Using Github as a CMS Backend
Description: Tim has offered to demonstrate some novel uses for the Github API, and how you can extend it into far reaching places. Some may not use it, but Github has a fairly decent CRUD GUI, and a great API. Tim wants to show you that you can avoid building your own CRUD and Enable server-less CMS functionality with markdown and revisions in git.

Title: Service Workers: Annoying or Helpful?
Description: A service worker is a script that your browser runs in the background, separate from a web page. This opens the door to features that don't need a web page or user interaction. Now, with a little bit of imagination, you can see how annoying or how useful service workers can be. Thiago will give us a tour of some of the features and annoyances of this piece of technology.

Title: Single Page Applications with ASP.NET Core
Description: Jason will be showing how we can use ASP.NET Core JavaScript Services to build single page applications using Angular, Aurelia, Knockout, React, React+Redux or Vue. He'll demonstrate server-side pre-rendering, webpack dev middleware, hot module replacement (HMR), efficient production builds and much more. You will walk away ready to create single page applications using your favourite client-side framework and ASP.NET Core.

Title: RxJS Debugging and Visualisation
Description: Frustrated by the poor tooling available for RxJS apps, Nicholas made rxjs-spy. It's been very useful with NgRx, and Slack's engineering team have adopted it with redux-observable apps. Nicholas will cover the problems this tool solves, how it works, use cases, and DevTools integrations.

Title: Why Ember?
Description: Contributing to the Ember presence in the Brisbane user group scene,  Kartik has kindly offered to answer the very question - Why Ember? He'll  endeavour to tell you how the Emberjs framework stacks up to a  multitude of other JavaScript frameworks out there and why you would  choose it over another.

Title: Lightning talk: Adventure & Discovery at Fronteers Conf
Description: The venerable Ash was a speaker at Fronteers (https://fronteers.nl/congres/2017/speakers#ash-kyd)  this year - and also had a great time being immersed in tech and the  Amsterdam nexus of the web interested minds. He'll be along to tell us  briefly about the cool things he learned/saw while there and tell you  what's hip and new in european JS. ;-)

Title: Turning syntax coloring off
Description: Syntax colouring is considered unquestionable for programmers. What  happens if your turn it off? After hearing about a number of high  profile programmers who choose not to use syntax colouring, Brandon  decided to banish it from his life, recorded the results, and will be  discussing what he learned during the process. It's through these  insights he can help to teach us how syntax colouring changes the way  programmers work.

Title: How I learned to stop worrying and love charting North Korean missile ranges in D3.js
Description: Josh joined the ABC's Digital Storytelling Team a little over 6  months ago as his first proper programming gig. Since then he's learned a  bunch of stuff, and published one of last year's most impressive  stories, drawing acclaim from Reddit and around the world. In this talk he'll take us on his learning journey and go through how to get off the ground with D3.

Title: Pair Programming
Description: Pair programming is a great way to bring newbies up to speed and even hone your own skills. In this lightning talk Caitlin shares her experiences, and 6 key tips to success.

Title: Filling up on polyfills
Description: You may have head of polyfills, but what the heck is a ponyfill? And how does that relate to a prollyfill? Find out all this and more in Kartik's 6 minute lightning talk!

Title: A fully asynchronous expression language
Description: The one where Kory Nunn does a lightning talk on PResh, a new totally asynchronous, functional, stateless, easy to add scope to, expressive, programming language.

Title: Bad Estimates: how one weekend blew out to 2.5 years (and a career change)
Description: Julian offered to give a shortened version of his much anticipated talk (and made us all wish we could see the full version!)

Title: 📰 Experiences working as a fellow at the ABC
Description: The Google News Lab Fellowship offers those interested in journalism  & technology the opportunity to spend the summer working at relevant  organizations across the world. We'll hear how Zoe got involved, and  what it's like working on data journalism at the ABC.

Title: 🐦 Flappy Bird under 5 minutes
Description: Flappy Bird will save you from boredom for about 5 minutes at a time.  Instead of playing it, Lochlan will attempt to build it from scratch!  Will he succeed?

Title: 👩‍💻 NodeGirls & the traits of a good mentor
Description: Anwesha is promoting the upcoming NodeGirls workshop (http://bit.ly/nodegirlsmarch18)  looking for mentors and attendees. As part of this we'll learn what  makes a good mentor, and how you can support and teach those around you.

Title: Building Static Sites with React
Description: React is great for client side applications, but has a heavy upfront  performance cost. So what if your site doesn't need to run a single page  app? Tim will show us how to scaffold a website using Create React App,  hook it up to content from a CMS and deploy as a static website on AWS  S3.

Title: What is TensorFlow JS?
Description: Google has just released TensorFlow JS and yes, its an AI thing for  Javascript. But what does it mean, what's it good for, and how can I get  started doing something with it?

Title: I created a new design pattern!
Description: Armagan currently works at Red Hat as a software engineer and enjoys  developing web-based systems with JS. She is also organiser of NodeGirls  Brisbane. In this talk, we will learn the ins and outs of cross-domain  communication in Javascript.

Title: Performance tips for writing a text annotation editor
Description: Iian is developing The Codex, a Neo4j digital humanities project aiming to create an atlas of events from primary sources from the Italian Renaissance. In this talk we'll hear a little about what he's up to, and some performance tips encountered along the way.

Title: JS & Accessibility
Description: We haven't had an accessibility talk at BrisJS since the meetup started,  so Larene is boldly going to break this tradition by discussing the  basics, and how they might apply to React. We ran a poll to see what  people wanted to hear, check it out here: https://twitter.com/BrisJS/status/992259606435909633

Title: Fixed Mindset vs Growth Mindset
Description: A short presentation on the damaging effects of a fixed mindset and how you can foster a growth mindset in development and other areas of life.

Title: The Top Five Internet JavaScripts this Month - you won’t BELIEVE #4!
Description: Where did that month go? Who cares - here’s your chance to blink and  miss it all over again as Josh Wulf covers the top five JavaScript  internets of the month in five minutes.

Title: Rad Or Bad? The Javascript quiz with Kory Nunn
Description: Are you across the latest JS features? In this special feature Kory  throws the question to the panel, who will channel the zeitgeist and  determine which features are worth your time, and which are there for  show.  (To check out what we'll be discussing and have your say, submit Kory's survey in advance https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/SMQG9V9)

Title: Decoding Design
Description: Given that there are about 22 million developers in the world, it is likely that the billions of regular tappers and swipers of the world will not at all be just like you. Building a product for people like you, therefore, greatly limits the size of your total addressable market - which in short, is really bad business. We know that startups co-founded by designers are far more likely to succeed. But why is this? What exactly do these mysterious Design Creatures do, and more importantly, what can you learn from them to help your product win the tapping and swiping game? How can your development work succeed in the market?

Title: Fast functional frontends in Elm and Javascript
Description: Elm is a lightweight functional language for the browser that compiles to javascript. Most elm tutorials show you a hello world or a small single page app and leave you at that. This presentation gives a brief introduction to elm and then  "heavyweight javascript" code such as oAuth providers, and mapping engines.dives in to how to integrate with existing "heavyweight javascript" code such as oAuth providers, and mapping engines.
